examples.en: The puppet danced in the puppet show.
He is just the boss's puppet.

examples.ko: 나는 누구의 꼭두각시도 되고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to be anyone's puppet.
I looked at traditional puppets at the museum.
Don't just do as you're told like a puppet.

examples.ko: 그 회사 대표를 꼭두각시라고 부르는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An article came out calling the company's CEO a puppet.

explain: 줄이나 막대로 움직이는 전통 인형을 말하고, 비유로 남이 시키는 대로만 움직이는 사람을 가리킬 때도 많이 써요. 비유로 쓰면 비난하는 느낌이 강해서 사람 앞에서 말할 때는 조심해야 해요. 영어의 puppet처럼 쓰는 거예요.

phrases.en: I bought a small puppet at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전통 인형이라는 원래 뜻으로 쓸 때 많이 붙이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly added when using the original meaning of a traditional puppet.

phrases.en: He only does what he is told, like a puppet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 결정하지 못하는 사람을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a comparison for someone who can't decide for themselves.

phrases.example: 저는 더 이상 꼭두각시 노릇을 하기 싫어요.
phrases.en: I don't want to play the puppet anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 조종당하는 역할을 하는 것을 말하고 비난하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means playing the role of someone controlled by others, with a critical tone.

explain_en: It refers to a traditional puppet moved by strings or sticks, and is also widely used figuratively for a person who only does what others tell them. Used figuratively it sounds quite accusing, so be careful saying it to someone. It works like the English word 'puppet'.

examples.ko: 사람을 겉모습만 보고 낮잡아 보면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't look down on people just by their appearance.
We underestimated the other team and lost badly.
Please don't underestimate me just because I'm young.

examples.ko: 남을 낮잡는 말투는 듣는 사람 기분을 상하게 해요.
examples.en: A tone that belittles others upsets the listener.

examples.ko: 처음엔 신입이라고 낮잡았는데 일을 정말 잘하더라고요.
examples.en: At first I underestimated him as a newbie, but he works really well.

examples.ko: 제 실력을 너무 낮잡아 말하지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't talk down your own ability so much.

explain: '얕보다', '깔보다'와 비슷하게 사람의 실력이나 가치를 실제보다 낮게 평가한다는 뜻이에요. '낮잡아 보다', '낮잡아 말하다'처럼 '-아/어'형으로 많이 써요. 반대로 높게 평가할 때는 '높이 평가하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Don't look down on someone just because they're a child.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낮잡다'가 가장 자주 쓰이는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form in which 낮잡다 appears.

phrases.en: Don't underestimate your opponent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령으로 충고할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give advice as a negative command.

phrases.en: I underestimated that team and lost.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낮잡다'와 비슷하고 말할 때 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 낮잡다 and more common in speech.

explain_en: Like '얕보다' and '깔보다', it means to rate someone's ability or worth lower than it really is. It is often used in the '-아/어' form, as in '낮잡아 보다' and '낮잡아 말하다'. The opposite, rating highly, is '높이 평가하다'.

examples.ko: 친구들의 놀림감이 되는 건 정말 싫어요.
examples.en: I really hate being the butt of my friends' jokes.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 이름 때문에 놀림감으로 자주 불렸어요.
examples.en: That child was often teased because of his name.
My mistake was the target of jokes all day.
You shouldn't make your younger sibling a laughingstock.

examples.ko: 별것 아닌 일로 놀림감 취급을 받았어요.
examples.en: I was treated like a joke over something trivial.

examples.ko: 내가 우스운 놀림감 같아서 기분이 나빴어요.
examples.en: I felt bad, as if I were some funny object of mockery.

explain: '놀림감이 되다', '놀림감으로 삼다'처럼 자주 써요. 비슷한 '웃음거리'는 남이 비웃는다는 느낌이 더 강하고, 놀림감은 누가 장난으로 놀린다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: Because of my mistake, I became the butt of my friends' jokes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남들이 장난으로 놀리는 대상이 될 때 가장 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say one becomes the target of teasing.
phrases.en_equiv: to become a target of teasing

phrases.en: Don't make your younger sibling a target of teasing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가를 일부러 놀리는 대상으로 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when deliberately making someone the target of teasing.
phrases.en_equiv: to make a target of teasing

phrases.en: I became a laughingstock because of that.
phrases.nuance_ko: '놀림감'과 비슷하지만 남이 비웃는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar but with a stronger sense of being laughed at.

explain_en: It is often used as '놀림감이 되다' (become a target of teasing) or '놀림감으로 삼다' (make someone a target). The similar '웃음거리' feels more like being laughed at, while 놀림감 feels like being teased for fun.

examples.ko: 저는 평범한 봉급쟁이라서 집 사기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: I'm an ordinary salaried worker, so buying a house is hard.
For salaried workers, taxes come straight out of the paycheck.
My father also worked as a salaried employee for a long time.

examples.ko: 봉급쟁이 생활이 지겨워서 가게를 열고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'm tired of the salaried life and want to open a shop.
Do you know how it feels to be a salaryman who only waits for payday?
I heard salaried workers worry a lot about the cost of lunch.

explain: 월급을 받고 일하는 직장인을 조금 낮추거나 스스로를 낮춰 말하는 느낌이 있어요. 같은 뜻으로 '월급쟁이'도 많이 쓰고, 중립적인 말은 '직장인'이에요. 남에게 쓰면 실례일 수 있으니 조심하세요.

phrases.en: Salaried workers end up waiting for payday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '봉급쟁이'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning as '봉급쟁이' and more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: I'm just an ordinary salaried worker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자신을 낮추어 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when humbly describing yourself.

phrases.en: After years as a salaried worker, I miss traveling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생활'을 붙여 직장인으로 사는 삶을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '생활' describes life as an office worker.

explain_en: It carries a slightly humble or belittling tone, often used for oneself. '월급쟁이' is also used with the same meaning, and the neutral word is '직장인'. Be careful using it about other people, since it can sound rude.

examples.en: My younger sibling is showing off with a new bag on.

examples.ko: 시험 한 번 잘 봤다고 너무 뻐기지 마요.
examples.en: Don't brag so much just because you did well on one test.
He goes around bragging about how much money he has.
People who show off don't have many friends.
My older brother bragged about coming first, and it was annoying.
Please don't talk as if you're showing off.

explain: '자랑하다'는 좋은 뜻으로도 쓰지만, '뻐기다'는 잘난 척하며 거만하게 구는 느낌이 있어서 늘 부정적이에요. '뻐기+어'가 줄어서 '뻐겨요', '뻐겼어요'가 돼요. 보통 남이 그러는 걸 보고 얄밉다고 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: The way he shows off is really annoying.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뻐기다'의 활용형으로, 잘난 척하는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form used for someone's smug, showing-off behavior.

phrases.example: 친구가 상을 받았다고 하루 종일 뻐겼어요.
phrases.en: My friend bragged all day about winning a prize.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 이미 거만하게 군 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for someone who already acted arrogantly.

phrases.example: 형이 새 신발을 신고 뻐기면서 걸어요.
phrases.en: My older brother walks around showing off his new shoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-면서'를 붙이면 뻐기면서 다른 행동을 하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-myeonseo' shows doing another action while showing off.

explain_en: '자랑하다' can be positive, but '뻐기다' always sounds negative, as if someone acts arrogant and full of themselves. '뻐기+어' contracts to '뻐겨요' and '뻐겼어요'. You usually use it when you find someone else's showing off annoying.

examples.en: The heir to that company is the eldest son.
The heir's name was written in the will.
Heirs of rich families often appear in dramas.
The heirs had a big fight over the property.
My grandfather left the house to his heir.
The court decided who the heir was.

explain: '상속인'은 법에서 쓰는 말이고, 상속자는 뉴스와 드라마에서 더 쉽게 써요. 재산뿐 아니라 회사 같은 가업을 이어받을 사람에게도 말해요. 물려주는 사람은 어렵고 법적인 말로 '피상속인'이에요.

phrases.en: The heir has to prepare the documents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법이나 서류에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word used in law and official papers.

phrases.en: He became the heir to his father's company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물려받을 사람이 정해졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person to inherit has been decided.

phrases.en: That child is the only heir.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상속받을 사람이 한 명뿐일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there is only one person to inherit.

explain_en: 상속인 is the legal term, while 상속자 is easier to hear in news and dramas. It is used not only for property but also for the person who will take over a family business such as a company. The person who passes it on is the formal legal term 피상속인.

examples.en: He is a leader of the eco-friendly movement.
To become a pioneer, you first need courage.
Our company is called a leader in the industry.

examples.ko: 새로운 유행의 선도자는 대개 젊은 사람들이에요.
examples.en: The trendsetters of a new fashion are usually young people.

examples.ko: 선도자의 길은 쉽지 않지만 보람이 커요.
examples.en: The path of a pioneer isn't easy, but it is very rewarding.

examples.ko: 그녀를 문화 운동의 선도자라고 부르는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people call her a leading figure of the cultural movement.

explain: '선구자'와 비슷하지만 선도자는 앞장서서 다른 사람들을 이끄는 모습에 더 초점이 있어요. 동사 '선도하다'와 같이 기억하면 쉬워요. 업계나 유행, 운동 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: She became a leader of the environmental movement.
phrases.nuance_ko: '되다'와 함께 써서 앞장서는 역할을 맡게 됐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 되다, it means taking on the role of leading the way.

phrases.example: 이 회사는 업계에서 선도자 역할을 해요.
phrases.en: This company plays a leading role in the industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조직이나 사람이 하는 일을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain the role of an organization or person.

phrases.en: Our team leads the new trend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '선도자'와 짝으로 외우면 좋은 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb worth learning together with the noun 선도자.

explain_en: It is close to '선구자', but 선도자 focuses more on the one who steps ahead and leads others. It is easy to remember together with the verb '선도하다'. It often appears when talking about industries, trends and movements.

examples.ko: 그는 선무당이라서 아는 척하다가 일을 망쳤어요.
examples.en: He only half knows things, and by pretending to know he ruined the job.

examples.ko: 선무당 같은 사람이 조언하면 오히려 위험해요.
examples.en: Advice from someone who only half knows is actually risky.
The half-informed amateur is the scariest.

examples.ko: 저는 선무당이라 이 일을 맡기가 겁나요.
examples.en: I'm only half skilled, so I'm afraid to take on this job.
I trusted only an amateur's word and spent a lot of money.

examples.ko: 인터넷 정보만 믿는 선무당이 되지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't become a half-informed amateur who only trusts internet information.

explain: 원래는 굿을 서투르게 하는 무당이지만, 요즘은 어설프게 아는 사람을 놀리거나 걱정할 때 비유로 써요. 듣는 사람에 따라 기분이 나쁠 수 있어서 남에게 직접 쓰는 건 조심해야 해요.

phrases.example: 조금 아는 걸로 약을 권했다가 큰일 날 뻔했어요. 선무당이 사람 잡는다더니!
phrases.en: I almost caused a disaster by recommending medicine based on a little knowledge. They say a half-skilled person does harm!
phrases.nuance_ko: 어설프게 아는 사람이 나서서 일을 크게 망친다는 속담이에요. 자기 자신을 반성할 때도, 남을 경고할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb saying that a person with only a little skill makes things worse by stepping in. You can use it to reflect on yourself or to warn others.
phrases.en_equiv: A little knowledge is a dangerous thing

explain_en: It originally means an unskilled shaman, but today it is used figuratively for someone who knows just a little, either teasingly or as a worry. It can offend, so be careful about saying it directly to someone.

examples.ko: 두 팀 감독이 경기 전부터 신경전을 벌였어요.
examples.en: The two team managers played mind games even before the match.
The department head and the section chief had a tense standoff in the meeting.

examples.ko: 가격을 두고 두 회사 사이에 신경전이 심해요.
examples.en: There's a heated war of nerves between the two companies over the price.

examples.ko: 형제가 리모컨을 두고 작은 신경전을 벌여요.
examples.en: The brothers have a little tussle over the remote control.
Before an election the candidates' sparring gets heated.
The mood was heavy because of the tension between them.

explain: '신경전'은 싸우지는 않지만 말이나 행동으로 서로 기싸움을 하는 상황에 써요. 보통 '신경전을 벌이다'로 말하고, 스포츠 뉴스나 회사 이야기에 자주 나와요. 몸이나 큰 소리로 맞붙는 다툼과 달리, 서로 눈치를 보며 긴장을 만드는 데 초점이 있어요.

phrases.example: 결승전 전에 두 선수 사이에 신경전이 벌어졌어요.
phrases.en: A war of nerves broke out between the two players before the final.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신경전을 벌이다'와 짝이 되는 표현이에요. 신경전이 저절로 시작된 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of 신경전을 벌이다, with the feeling that the tussle just started on its own.
phrases.en_equiv: a war of nerves breaks out

phrases.example: 계약을 두고 두 회사가 치열한 신경전을 벌였어요.
phrases.en: The two companies waged a fierce war of nerves over the contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신경전이 아주 심할 때 '치열한'을 앞에 붙여요. 보통 '벌이다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 치열한 before it when the tussle is very intense. It is usually used with 벌이다.

phrases.example: 처음 만난 두 사람이 기싸움을 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The two people who just met are in a battle of wills.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신경전'과 뜻이 비슷하지만 서로 기세를 누르려는 느낌이 더 강하고 구어에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 신경전 but with a stronger sense of trying to overpower the other, and common in speech.

explain_en: '신경전' is for a standoff where people do not fight openly but test each other with words and attitude. The usual pairing is '신경전을 벌이다', and it is common in sports news and workplace talk. Unlike a physical or shouting quarrel, the focus is on building tension while watching each other.

examples.en: That director is a rising newcomer in the film world.

examples.ko: 신예 작가의 첫 소설이 베스트셀러가 됐어요.
examples.en: The young writer's first novel became a bestseller.

examples.ko: 이번 대회에는 신예 선수들이 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Many up-and-coming players took part in this competition.
This year's rookie award went to a rising star of the theater world.

examples.ko: 신예 가수 중에서 누구를 가장 좋아해요?
examples.en: Among the up-and-coming singers, who do you like the most?

examples.ko: 그 팀은 신예와 베테랑이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: On that team, the rising stars and the veterans work well together.

explain: '신인'은 막 시작한 사람이면 누구나 가리키지만, '신예'는 새로 나타났는데 실력이 눈에 띈다는 느낌이 있어요. 작가, 감독, 선수 앞에 붙이거나 '신예로 떠오르다'처럼 뉴스와 기사에서 자주 보여요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '베테랑', '노장'이에요.

phrases.example: 그 신예 작가는 첫 책으로 큰 상을 받았어요.
phrases.en: That up-and-coming writer won a big prize with their first book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 나왔지만 실력이 눈에 띄는 작가를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to a writer who is new but already stands out for talent.

phrases.example: 신예 선수가 경기에서 멋진 골을 넣었어요.
phrases.en: The rising young player scored a great goal in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 기사에서 주목받는 새 선수를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is often used in sports news for a new player who attracts attention.

phrases.en: That singer emerged as a rising star this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 주목받기 시작했다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means someone suddenly began to get attention, and it is common in the news.
phrases.en_equiv: to emerge as a rising star

explain_en: '신인' simply means someone who has just started, but '신예' also suggests that the person stands out for their talent. It is often attached before writers, directors and athletes, or used like '신예로 떠오르다' in news articles. The opposite feeling is '베테랑' or '노장'.

examples.ko: 처음에는 오합지졸이었던 우리 팀이 이제는 꽤 강해졌어요.
examples.en: Our team, which started out as a rabble, has gotten quite strong now.

examples.ko: 연습 한 번 안 하고 나가면 오합지졸처럼 보일 거예요.
examples.en: If you go out without practicing even once, you'll look like a rabble.

examples.ko: 감독님은 선수들을 오합지졸이라고 부르며 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: The coach got angry and called the players a bunch of rabble.

examples.ko: 오합지졸 같은 군대로는 큰 전쟁을 이길 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't win a big war with an army that is just a rabble.

examples.ko: 모인 사람은 많은데 다들 따로 놀아서 오합지졸이에요.
examples.en: Lots of people showed up, but everyone does their own thing, so it's a rabble.

examples.ko: 오합지졸로 시작했지만 우리는 끝까지 포기하지 않았어요.
examples.en: We started as a rabble, but we never gave up until the end.

explain: 군대뿐 아니라 팀이나 모임처럼 준비 없이 모인 사람들에게도 써요. 조금 비꼬는 말투라서 상대방에게 직접 말하면 무례할 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 준비가 안 돼서 우리 모임이 오합지졸 같아요.
phrases.en: We're not prepared, so our group is like a disorganized mob.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조직이 엉성하고 모여만 있을 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for a loosely organized group.

phrases.en: Without a leader, we turn into a disorganized mob.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질서 없이 모인 무리가 된다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means turning into a group gathered without order.

phrases.en: If we go out without uniforms, we'll look like a ragtag crowd.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 엉성해 보인다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means looking disorganized from the outside.

explain_en: It is used not only for armies but also for teams or groups that gathered without preparation. It has a slightly sarcastic tone, so saying it directly to someone can be rude.

examples.en: That player is an idol to children.
Many fans follow the singer like an idol.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 우상이었던 배우를 직접 만났어요.
examples.en: I met in person the actor who was my idol as a child.
Making an idol and worshipping it is dangerous.
My idol is someone who always makes an effort.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 도시 사람들의 우상으로 불려요.
examples.en: That team is called the idol of the city's people.

explain: 존경하고 열광하며 따르는 사람을 말할 때 써요. 닮고 싶은 사람은 '롤모델'이라고 하고, '우상'은 더 열광하는 느낌이에요. 종교에서 섬기는 조각상도 '우상'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That actor became an idol to teenagers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많은 사람이 열광하는 대상이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone becomes a figure many people adore.

phrases.en: I look up to my older brother as my idol.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신이 따르는 사람으로 정한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means choosing someone as the person you follow.

phrases.en: Some religions forbid idol worship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종교에서 조각상을 섬기는 일을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to worshipping images or statues in religion.

explain_en: Used for a person you admire and follow with great enthusiasm. A person you want to be like is a '롤모델', while 우상 feels more passionate. In religion, a worshipped statue is also called 우상.

examples.ko: 영화에서 그는 도시를 부수는 파괴자로 나와요.
examples.en: In the movie he appears as a destroyer who smashes the city.

examples.ko: 환경 파괴자라는 말을 들으면 마음이 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts to be called an environmental destroyer.

examples.ko: 게임 속 파괴자는 힘이 아주 센 캐릭터예요.
examples.en: The destroyer in the game is a very strong character.
That company is called a disruptor of the market.
They are investigating who the destroyer of the forest is.
Children are little wreckers who break toys.

explain: '파괴자'는 물건, 자연, 질서를 부수는 사람이나 존재예요. 'ㅇㅇ 파괴자'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여 '환경 파괴자', '평화 파괴자'로 자주 써요. 장난으로 말하면 귀엽게 들리지만, 진지하게 쓰면 강한 비난이 돼요.

phrases.en: He was called a destroyer of the village's peace.
phrases.nuance_ko: '평화'를 앞에 붙여 무엇을 부수는 사람인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 평화 in front to say what the person destroys.

phrases.en: People who cut in line are wreckers of order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이나 순서를 지키지 않는 사람을 강하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A strong way to describe someone who ignores rules or order.

phrases.example: 작은 거짓말이 신뢰의 파괴자가 될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: A small lie can become a destroyer of trust.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람뿐 아니라 어떤 일이 나쁜 결과를 만든다는 비유로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used figuratively for things that cause bad results.

explain_en: 파괴자 is a person or being that destroys things, nature, or order. It often follows a target word, as in 환경 파괴자 or 평화 파괴자. Said jokingly it can sound cute, but said seriously it is a strong accusation.

examples.en: I'm still a rookie who isn't good at the job yet.
I made a lot of mistakes when I was a newbie.

examples.ko: 풋내기라고 해도 열정은 누구에게도 지지 않아요.
examples.en: Even though I'm a novice, I'm second to none in passion.
Though a rookie, the player stayed calm in the game.
A greenhorn reporter landed a big scoop.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에는 풋내기들이 많아서 분위기가 밝아요.
examples.en: Our team has many newcomers, so the mood is bright.

explain: '초보자'보다 경험이 적고 서툴러 보이는 사람이라는 느낌이 있어서, 남이 말하면 얕잡아 보는 말처럼 들릴 수 있어요. 자기 자신을 낮춰 말할 때는 괜찮아요. 중립적으로 말하려면 '초보', '신입'을 쓰세요.

phrases.en: I'm still a beginner driver.
phrases.nuance_ko: '풋내기'보다 중립적이라 남에게도 편하게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More neutral than 풋내기, so it's fine to use about other people.

phrases.en: I'm new here, so there's a lot I don't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 모임에 새로 들어온 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone newly joined to a company or group.

phrases.en: I'm still a novice, so I have a lot to learn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자신을 낮춰 말할 때 자연스러운 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural conjugated form when humbly describing yourself.

explain_en: Compared with '초보자', it suggests someone with little experience who looks unskilled, so it can sound belittling when others say it. It is fine for describing yourself modestly. For a neutral tone, use '초보' or '신입'.

examples.en: The war created many evacuees.
The evacuees are staying in temporary shelters.
The school became a shelter for evacuees.
Volunteers handed out blankets to the evacuees.
Some evacuees lost their homes in the flood.

examples.ko: 피난민 아이들이 새 학교에 다니기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The evacuee children started attending a new school.

explain: 전쟁이나 재난의 위험을 피해 살던 곳을 떠난 사람에게 써요. 나라 밖으로 피한 사람은 '난민'을 더 많이 써요. 홍수나 지진으로 집을 잃은 사람은 '이재민'이라고도 해요. 한국전쟁 이야기에도 '피난민'이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The flood created many evacuees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재난이나 전쟁 뒤에 사람들이 떠나게 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means people were forced to leave after a disaster or war.

phrases.en: Volunteers help the evacuees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움이나 구호 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in talk about aid and relief.

phrases.en: My grandfather was a war refugee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일 때문에 피난한 사람인지 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The cause of fleeing is put in front.

explain_en: It refers to people who left home to escape the danger of war or disaster. For people who fled abroad, '난민' is used more. People who lost homes to floods or earthquakes are also called '이재민'. '피난민' often appears in stories about the Korean War.
